restrictions: Target sha256-r39-prefix-v1: SHA-256 reduced to its first 39 steps in every compression, FIPS 180-4 padding, the standard IV, feed-forward, equality of all eight 32-bit digest words. Output: two distinct 128-byte messages M0 || M1 and M0 || M1' with the same random first block M0 and second blocks that give equal chaining values; the padding block that follows is identical, so the digests are equal. The cost is the work of the program experiments/r39joint.py over B first blocks, one window of 2^26 walk evaluations each.

Construction, credited: sraiw's 38912d66 transplants a 39-step semi-free-start pair onto a random first-block chaining value through an exact bijection (cv, a0, a1) <-> (W8, W9, W16..W23); row 16 is the claw F(a0) = F(u), a0 even and u odd, of a 32-bit map, found by a van Oorschot-Wiener distinguished-point walk (dariolina's row-16 claw idea: 21b6653a, 2c48b18c, cfe5c4e2, 4e396742); then W8 in F8 and W9 in F9 (exact 585/524288), W17 = 0x71e9ba98 (2^-32 for uniform W17), and the tail rows 18 to 38 (p_tail). The contribution is a new signed 39-step characteristic (ePrint 2026/1120 Table 21 with W11 and W12 re-signed) and its pair, used as advice (proof Section 2.1, Appendix C). Declared dependencies: 44870635, bb21016d, 38912d66, 4e396742, 2c48b18c, cfe5c4e2, 744875ec, 0c1ef7c3, 6b678689.

Machine model (prices of this entry's cost model, proof Section 4), collision-frontier-v5: a counted 256-bit word RAM with 256 registers (counted as memory), 2812 operations per target compression. One operation each: XOR, AND, OR, NOT, move, shift, rotate, add, subtract, compare, set; a branch is a compare plus a branch (2); a load or a store is 3 (index shift, base add, access); a call plus its return is 2. A walk-kernel body record (register-to-register XOR, AND, OR or NOT, no immediate operand) is 5 bytes, the price of dariolina's 6b678689 and our 0c1ef7c3; every other instruction is 36 bytes. One executed WebAssembly operator of the in-program generator is one operation (it halts at 575,000 operators). Every operation of the program is counted by the class Mach; no price is an average.

time_log2 = 118.2659 is log2 of the charged-work budget plus one window, (W_BUDGET + R + 6 B) / 2812 target-compressions, with W_BUDGET = B x 628,007,505 x (1 + 2^-20): the 99% upper bound of the operations per window and B from the 99% lower bound of the distinct claws per window (proof Section 7; at the plain means it would be 118.2542). 12,360.2 operations per distinct claw is the count executed by the program over 24 windows of 2^26 walk evaluations on the real step function (1,213,630 distinct claws, 50,567.9 per window), in categories that add up to it (proof Section 5 and Appendix A). N = ln(1/0.61) / (p8 p9 2^-32 p_tail) / 0.99858 = 2^116.1202 distinct claws, p8 p9 = 585/524288, log2 p_tail = -75.327 (the measured mean of the 14 tail replica runs, H2-tail). The program halts after B = 2^100.4970 windows or at the charged-work budget 2^129.7232 (proof Section 7); its other halts (kernel image over 1030 records, over 206 registers, generator over 575,000 operators) are charged. Success probability 0.39.

Memory 1,047,548 bytes = 2^19.9986, claimed as 2^20: register file 8,192; 2 kernel images x 1030 x 5 = 10,300; 3,520 other instructions (759 census, 1,100 hand-counted routines, 1,661 generator and relocation) x 36 = 126,720; table 26,112 words x 32 = 835,584; lane array, save area, queue, pair slots, timing wheel, free stack and counters 66,592; advice 160. The generator's scratch lies in the table region during generation. No solver, no search campaign and no preprocessing buffer: setup and attack share this peak.

Advice and preprocessing: the advice is our 39-step semi-free-start pair (chaining value, M, M': 160 bytes) on a re-signed Table 21 characteristic, embedded in the program. Its offline construction is our characteristic-guided SAT instance (kissat, one core), charged at its timed replay: 1,499 s x 2^26 target compressions per core-second = 2^36.55, preprocessing_log2 = 37; construction memory at most 2^28 bytes (replay peak 156,286,976), one-time, ended before the attack starts (premise H3-base, proof Section 11). Attack memory 2^20. time_log2 is unchanged.

Experiments r39-transplant-claw and r39-window-small run experiments/r39joint.py in the organizer sandbox and return no message pair: r39-transplant-claw (the advice pair through claw(); the transplant identity on 255 random chaining values) and r39-window-small (one window cut to 2^22 evaluations, check mode). They are program checks; no number of this claim is estimated from their counts. The tail is replicated in the sandbox by experiments/r39tail.py (r39-tail-01..14, proof Sections 8 and 10). No outside code or library is used; the generator is compiled from the string GEN_C of the program file.

heuristics.statement: Four parts. (a) The chaining value cv of a random first block behaves as an independent random value for the walk map F and the later events, so the windows of the program are independent trials. (b) The yield and the cost of a window are those measured on the real step function over 24 full-size windows: 50,567.9 distinct claws and 12,360.2 operations per distinct claw; the program cannot be run for 2^100.8 windows. (c) A distinct claw (a0 even, u odd, F(a0) = F(u)) is, for the events W8 in F8, W9 in F9, W17 = 0x71e9ba98 and the tail, a trial with probability p8 p9 2^-32 p_tail, independent of the walk's yield, with p8 p9 = 585/524288 exact; claws are counted by groups with a shared endpoint (one claw per group suffices; groups/claws = 0.99858 over 6 windows). (d) W17 is uniform over the claws.
heuristics.scope: The fixed target sha256-r39-prefix-v1 and the program of experiments/r39joint.py: first blocks drawn uniformly, windows of 2^26 walk evaluations of the real step function F, claws with W16 = g by the construction with this entry's advice. Not claimed for another base pair, another round count or another walk.
heuristics.extrapolation: Our theory: the claws of the walk are uniform on the free words of the bijection (cv, a0, a1) <-> (W8, W9, W16..W23) apart from the claw equation. Measured on 310,224 real claws of 6 random first blocks (found by our C model of the same walk, not shipped): W9 in F9 5,015 (0.01617; expected 0.01587), W8 in F8 22,002 (0.07092; 0.07031), both 360 (0.001160; 0.001116); matches of W17 with 0x71e9ba98 in the low k bits, k = 8: 1,199 (1,211.8 expected), k = 12: 82 (75.7), k = 16: 5 (4.73), k = 20: 0 (0.30), k = 24: 0 (0.02); chi-square of the low 16 bits of W17 against uniform 65,830.2 on 65,535 degrees of freedom, z = 0.82. Part (b) is measured over 24 windows (window range 12,203 to 12,731 operations per claw, standard error of the mean 27.6) and extended to 2^100.9 windows by part (a). The windows and the claw test ran with the published pair as advice; the advice enters F only through the constant cw, which is uniform for a uniform cv (cv7 enters no other constant), so the per-window distribution is the same for this entry's advice (proof Section 9).
heuristics.limitations: The test of W17 covers its low 16 bits and the side-condition rates; the high 16 bits of W17, the independence of W17 from the tail event and the full 2^-32 are not testable at 310,224 claws and are the premise (d). Part (b) is a measurement over 24 windows, not a run of the full number of windows; its standard error is 0.22 percent (0.003 bit).

heuristics.statement: For the claws of the program (a0 even, u odd, W16 = g, W8 in F8, W9 in F9, W17 = 0x71e9ba98) the probability that the two 39-step compressions of the pair give equal 256-bit outputs is at least 2^-75.327, the quantity of proof Section 8 (rows 18 to 38, W18..W23 uniform); that quantity is at most the tail probability because the carrier K_P is a subset of all routes to a collision.
heuristics.scope: The tail rows 18 to 38 of the advice trail after the claw (the states of steps 12 to 17 equal the published ones), W8 uniform on F8, W9 uniform on F9, E18..E23 of the first member uniform on 2^32, a0 even and u odd. Not claimed for another trail.
heuristics.extrapolation: Our theory: p_tail >= 2^-75.327, declared at the measured mean. The organizer replica experiments/r39tail.py with this advice (r39-tail-01..14) gives, with the public seeds, 620 hits in 8,601,600 proposals, all verified collisions, mean log2 Q' = -75.327 over the 14 runs, standard error of the mean 4.9 percent (0.07 bit); reproducible observations consistent with the premise. This is the tail measured on this advice; no tail gain over the published advice is claimed.
heuristics.limitations: The declared value is the mean of 14 replica runs of an unbiased SMC estimator (sample: 620 verified hits in 8,601,600 proposals; standard error of the mean 4.9 percent (0.07 bit)). The replica draws W8, W9 uniformly in F8, F9 and does not test the walk's claw output (H1 part (c)); K_P is a subset of the routes to a collision.

heuristics.statement: The 160-byte advice (our chaining value, M, M' on the re-signed characteristic) is constructed offline by one run of our characteristic-guided SAT instance, charged at its timed replay, 1,499 s on one core, 1,499 x 2^26 = 2^36.55 target compressions (preprocessing_log2 = 37), construction memory at most 268,435,456 bytes = 2^28 (the replay peaked at 156,286,976 bytes); time_log2 is unchanged for any construction cost below 2^98.
heuristics.scope: The offline construction cost of this entry's 160-byte advice; nothing else.
heuristics.extrapolation: Measured: time and memory of the replay read by /usr/bin/time; the pair decoded from the assignment is verified as a 39-step collision from its chaining value (experiment r39-transplant-claw). The rate 2^26 target compressions per core-second is above what one core can execute (2^35 instructions x 3 word operations / 2812).
heuristics.limitations: A SAT solver has no a priori running-time bound; the charge is the measured run that produced the advice, which is a fixed 160-byte constant of the program.
